title: How can watermarks be embedded in generated text generated by LLMs?
question: This is a follow-up question to the original question. I didn't fully understand the original question and the discussion in the comments. How can I remove text watermarks from Claude output? So I would like to clarify how the watermark is technically embedded in the generated text generated by LLMs. What are the possible mechanisms or methods for embedding a watermark in generated text generated by LLMs?
answer: If you want to embed watermarks in your text generated by LLMs, there are three basic categories of methods: 1. The visible text itself Words Sentence structure Style Punctuation Word/order sequence Statistical properties 2. The character sequence underlying the visible representation Unicode variants Invisible characters Whitespace Control characters Homoglyphs Normalization variants 3. Information outside the actual text Metadata File information Cryptographic signatures The following are general ways someone could try to circumvent or make the different types your watermarking unrecognizable generated by LLMs?: 1. The visible text itself Write/review the text yourself Use your own wording and structure Avoid relying on automated rewriting Verify the content independently 2. The character sequence underlying the visible representation Normalize the text to a standard Unicode form Remove non-printing/control characters Validate and sanitize the character set Convert the text to a clean plain-text representation 3. Information outside the actual text Inspect metadata before sharing Remove unnecessary metadata Export the content as clean plain text when appropriate Check files for embedded provenance information
